text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Newspaper editorial attacks the opposition as too passive, saying it has recently failed to criticise the government's mistakes.
- Police have arrested over a dozen people, including members of the police forces, in the southern town of Berat in the past month in an effort to discover links between crime rings and police.
- The Italian foreign minister's envoy reminded Albanian political parties not to forget their dialogue.
- A parliamentary committee for economy, finances and budgetary matters is debating a presidential decree on the privatisation of state-owned banks.
- An alleged get-rich-quick pyramid scheme company is said to have deposited money it accumulated from people at a bank in Tirana.
- Lack of any law on private radio and television means anyone might launch them, an international seminar on the European convention of human rights and Albanian legislation said.
- The Albanian Football Association was reinstated by FIFA, world soccer's governing body, clearing the way for a World Cup qualifying match against Northern Ireland to go ahead.

- The U.S. deputy assistant secretary of State Steve Coffey in a Voice of America interview said all Albanian parties should decide on a new constitution, and called for greater press freedom. Washington would review bilateral relations, he added.
- President Sali Berisha lodged a complaint at the OSCE summit in Lisbon about the situation of the ethnic Albanians in the Serbian province of Kosovo.
- Scores of Albanians are sueing the president of a pyramid scheme company who is alleged to have fled the country with $13 million.
- Two ex-senior secret police officers, Irakli Kocollari and Vladimir Hysi, were sentenced to six and two years in jail respectively for abuse of power.
- Albania may resume its railway link with Montenegro, abandonned for the past five years, next Monday.
- Albania is to reconstruct its hydropower station of Vau i Dejes in northern Shkoder district within three years with a $16.2 million credit from World Bank.
- Albanian Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi praised the International Monetary Fund in a meeting with its representative in Albania Franz Drees, for assisting his country's economic development.
